You will also own the integration design connecting Oracle Fusion to Shopify for e-commerce order and inventory synchronization, and to the client'swarehouse management system(s) for outbound and inbound logistics â alongside integration with adjacent Oracle Fusion modules as applicable.

This is a nearshore delivery role, based in Mexico or Brazil, working in a remote-first model alongside Tessera's distributed FDE delivery and AI engineering teams. Because you will be running workshops and presenting directly tobusiness stakeholders and client leadership, excellent business English â spoken and written â is essential to this role.

Key Responsibilities

â¢ Lead and facilitate business process workshops with logistics, supply chain, procurement, and operations stakeholders to capture requirements for a greenfield Oracle Fusion Cloud implementation, spanning Inventory Management, Order Management, Indirect Procurement, and related logistics processes.

â¢ Own end-to-end functional configuration of Oracle Fusion modules â Inventory Management, Order

translating workshop outcomes into a working, standard-first system design.

title: Performance Marketing Manager (m/w/d) - Berlin
description:
Deine Mission

Du übernimmst die volle strategische und operative Verantwortung für unser Performance Marketing mit Fokus auf Meta und Google. Du entwickelst zusammen mit der Head of Marketing die Kanalstrategie, planst und verantwortest das Budget und sorgst für eine kontinuierliche Skalierung bei stabiler oder wachsender Effizienz.

Du arbeitest eng mit der Head of Marketing sowie Content/Design zusammen.

Diese Stelle entsteht im Zuge unserer nächsten Wachstumsphase, in der wir unser Marketing-Team ausbauen.

Aufgaben

Deine Aufgaben

  • Performance-Marketing-Strategie für Meta und Google eigenverantwortlich entwickeln, inklusive Budget-Forecasting und Kanal-Mix-Entscheidungen
  • Meta-Ads-Kampagnen eigenständig aufsetzen, skalieren und optimieren (Paid Facebook, Paid Instagram, Advantage+) inkl. strukturiertem Creative Testing auf Basis klarer Hypothesen
  • Google-Ads-Kampagnen über Performance Max, Search und GDN strategisch planen, skalieren und laufend optimieren (Smart-Bidding-Strategien, Asset-Gruppen, Audience Signals)
  • Ein systematisches Testing- und Measurement-Framework aufbauen, inklusive Incrementality Testing und sauberer Attribution über alle Kanäle hinweg
  • Server-seitiges Tracking und Conversion-Setups (u. a. Meta Conversions API, Google Enhanced Conversions) verantworten und kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln
  • Landingpages gemeinsam mit Content/Design kontinuierlich testen und auf Conversion optimieren
  • Unsere Tool-Landschaft (Pipedrive, Make, HeyFlow) mitgestalten und weiterentwickeln (von der Lead-Übergabe bis zur Automatisierung wiederkehrender Prozesse)
  • SEA-Maßnahmen eigenständig verantworten und SEO-Grundlagen im Blick behalten
  • Marketing-KPIs und Unit Economics (CTR, ROAS, CPL, MQL, Conversion Rate, Qualifikationsrate, CAC, LTV) laufend auswerten, forecasten und in Budget-Entscheidungen übersetzen

Qualifikation

Dein Talent

  • 4 bis 6 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Performance Marketing, davon mehrere Jahre in eigenverantwortlicher Rolle mit direkter Budgetverantwortung (idealerweise mit Stationen in Startups, Scaleups oder spezialisierten Performance-Agenturen)
  • Tiefe Hands-on-Erfahrung mit Meta Ads: Paid Facebook, Paid Instagram, Advantage+-Kampagnen, CBO/ABO-Strukturen
  • Tiefe Hands-on-Erfahrung mit Google Ads: Performance Max, Search, GDN, inklusive Smart-Bidding-Strategien sowie Asset-Gruppen- und Audience-Signal-Optimierung
  • Fundierte Erfahrung mit Tracking- und Measurement-Setups: GA4, Server-Side-Tracking, Conversions-API/Enhanced Conversions
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Marketing-KPIs und Unit Economics (CTR, ROAS, CPL, MQL, Conversion Rate, Qualifikationsrate, CAC, LTV) sowie Erfahrung im Forecasting von Budgets und Ergebnissen
  • Verständnis von Kreation sowie Erfahrung in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Design & Konzept

Benefits

Unser Angebot

💰 Attraktives Vergütungsmodell: Ein starkes, faires Fixgehalt – transparent und ohne versteckte Haken. Deine Leistung zahlt sich bei uns über Entwicklung und Verantwortung aus, nicht über ein kompliziertes Bonus-System.

🚀 Frisch finanziert, hier zu bleiben: Unbefristeter Vertrag in einem Unternehmen, das gerade 17,5 Mio. € Series A eingesammelt hat. Du bist nicht Mitarbeiter Nr. 200 in einem austauschbaren Konzern, sondern Teil des Teams, das die nächste Wachstumsphase baut.

🌍 Impact, den du zählen kannst: Jeder qualifizierte Lead wird am Ende zu einer Einblasdämmung, Kerndämmung oder Sparrendämmung in einem echten Haus – weniger Heizkosten für die Familie, weniger CO₂ für alle. Du verkaufst keine Software-Lizenz, du dämmst Deutschland.

🏢 Mitten in Kreuzberg: Unser Office am Paul-Lincke-Ufer, direkt am Landwehrkanal – hybrid, mit Homeoffice-Flexibilität, aber nah genug dran, dass man sich noch sieht.

🏖️ 30 Tage Urlaub: Volle 30 Tage. Ob langer Sommerurlaub, verlängertes Wochenende zwischendurch oder einfach mal drei Tage am Stück ohne Laptop: Bei uns musst du dir Erholung nicht erkämpfen.

🙏 Team statt nur Kollegen: Wir arbeiten hart am Ziel, verlernen dabei aber nicht das Miteinander. Regelmäßige Offsites bringen das ganze Team an einen Tisch, Team-Events sorgen für den informellen Austausch abseits vom Daily Business, und wer sportlich unterwegs sein will, ist beim Padel- oder Running-Club genau richtig. Und weil Wachstum ohne ehrliches Feedback nicht funktioniert, geben wir es dir laufend – direkt, konstruktiv und nicht erst im jährlichen Review-Gespräch.

🥤 Rundum versorgt: Siebträgermaschine für den Koffein-Nachschub, Softdrinks im Kühlschrank für zwischendurch, dazu Müslibar und Snacks für den kleinen Hunger am Nachmittag – alles kostenfrei und jederzeit verfügbar. Kein Grund, für die Basics extra ins Café um die Ecke zu laufen.

💻 Deine Wahl, dein Gerät: Ob MacBook oder Lenovo – du weißt am besten, womit du produktiv bist, also entscheidest du. Kein vorgegebenes Standardgerät, mit dem du dich erst arrangieren musst: Wir statten dich mit der Hardware aus, mit der du dich von Tag eins an wohlfühlst.

Über VARM

VARM ist eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Climate-Tech-Startups in Europa: Wir denken Wärmedämmung neu und unterstützen Eigenheimbesitzer:innen dabei, ihre Häuser energieeffizient zu modernisieren – einfach, digital und mit einem direkten Beitrag zur Energiewende.

Klingt nach einer perfekten Stelle für dich?

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung und darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

Auch wenn du unserem Anforderungsprofil nicht zu 100 % entsprichst, ermutigen wir dich trotzdem, dich bei uns zu bewerben.

VARM ist ein Arbeitgeber, der Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt fördert. Wir bemühen uns, ein freundliches, sicheres und einladendes Umfeld für alle unsere Mitarbeiter*innen zu schaffen, unabhängig von ethnischer Herkunft, Geschlecht, Geschlechtsidentität und -ausdruck, sexueller Orientierung, Einschränkungen und Begabungen jeglicher Art, körperlicher Erscheinung, sozialem Hintergrund, Familienstand, Alter oder Religion (oder deren Fehlen).

title: Senior BI Developer (m/w/d)
description:
Für ein etabliertes, technologieorientiertes Unternehmen suchen wir im Rahmen der Direktvermittlung über PRIME HR Agentur® einen erfahrenen Senior BI Developer (m/w/d) mit Schwerpunkt auf Microsoft Fabric, Power BI und Azure.

Neben klassischen BI-Lösungen spielen dabei auch KI-gestützte Anwendungen, Automatisierungen, Bots, Copilots und AI Agents eine zunehmend wichtige Rolle.

  • Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Kunden und/oder fachlichen Stakeholdern

  • Erfahrung in agilen Entwicklungsumgebungen und der Arbeit mit User Stories, Aufwandsschätzungen und Sprint-Zielen
  • Kenntnisse in Git und modernen kollaborativen Entwicklungsprozessen
  • Erfahrung mit Testing, Deployment und Betrieb produktiver Datenlösungen
  • Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
  • Einen routinierten und verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit modernen KI-Tools wie beispielsweise Copilot, Claude, Cursor, Codex oder vergleichbaren Lösungen

  • Erfahrung darin, KI-Prototypen in sichere und langfristig wartbare Produktivlösungen zu überführen
  • Kenntnisse in Databricks
  • Erfahrung mit Python oder PySpark
  • Gute Deutschkenntnisse ab B2-Niveau
  • Erfahrung in einem kundenorientierten Projektumfeld
  • Bereitschaft, technologische Entwicklungen aktiv zu verfolgen und gewonnene Erkenntnisse mit dem Team zu teilen

Benefits

  • Direkter Austausch mit Kunden und die Möglichkeit, eigene technische Themen maßgeblich voranzutreiben

  • Sie übernehmen die laufende buchhalterische Betreuung mehrerer Gesellschaften aus dem Fonds- und Immobilienbereich, insbesondere in den Rechtsformen GmbH und GmbH & Co. KG.

  • Darüber hinaus erstellen Sie Ergebnisprognosen, Hochrechnungen und aussagekräftige Plan-Ist-Analysen.
  • Bei bilanziellen oder buchhalterischen Fragestellungen stehen Sie im Austausch mit Wirtschaftsprüfern, Geschäftspartnern sowie internen Ansprechpartnern.
  • Sie wirken aktiv bei der Klärung und Lösung komplexerer Sachverhalte mit und sorgen für eine verlässliche Zahlenbasis.

Qualifikation

  • Sie verfügen über eine abgeschlossene Qualifikation als Bilanzbuchhalter (IHK) (m/w/d) oder eine Ausbildung zum Steuerfachangestellten (m/w/d).
  • Idealerweise bringen Sie bereits mehrere Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Finanz- und Rechnungsbuchhaltung mit.
  • Sie beherrschen die relevanten Bereiche der Buchhaltung – von Sachkonten über Debitoren und Kreditoren bis hin zur Anlagenbuchhaltung.

  • Kenntnisse im Bereich KAGB bzw. der Rechnungslegung von Fonds- und Kapitalverwaltungsgesellschaften sind ein Plus.
  • Mit den gängigen MS-Office-Anwendungen arbeiten Sie routiniert. Erfahrungen mit SAP sind von Vorteil.
  • Eine gewissenhafte, strukturierte und eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise zeichnet Sie aus.
  • Sie arbeiten gerne im Team, sind zuverlässig und behalten auch bei anspruchsvollen Themen den Überblick.
  • Neue Aufgabenstellungen gehen Sie pragmatisch und lösungsorientiert an.

Benefits

  • Ein abwechslungsreiches Tätigkeitsfeld mit anspruchsvollen Aufgaben im Fonds- und Immobilienumfeld.
  • Eine attraktive Vergütung sowie zusätzliche Leistungen zur Unterstützung Ihrer privaten Altersvorsorge.
  • Ein strukturierter Onboarding-Prozess mit umfassender Einarbeitung und fachlicher Unterstützung durch erfahrene Kolleginnen und Kollegen.

title: Pricing & Deal Desk Manager (m/f/d)
description:
At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions.

Our team and culture make us unique — we’re driven by impact and growth, where every one of us strives to learn and excel. Recognised by Sifted’s Rising 100 and LinkedIn's Top Startups, we’re here to help propel your career and together, make Moss a lasting success.

We're hiring a Pricing & Deal Desk Manager within the Revenue Operations team. You'd take ownership of one of Moss's highest-leverage commercial functions: the pricing deal desk. It's already delivered real results, and it matters more every quarter as deal volume grows and Moss moves into bigger, more complex deals.

What makes the role unusual is that the desk already runs on AI. An agent picks up each request, pulls the deal's scoring and call history, calculates margin, and drafts a reasoned reply; you approve, correct, or overrule it. So the job is two things at once: the reviewer who decides live deals, and the person who builds & improves the AI-based deal desk agent

Your responsibilities

  • Own the day-to-day approval flow for non-standard pricing, discounts, and commercial terms, acting as the fast, consistent escalation point for reps without slowing deals down.

  • Build and evolve pricing governance, including discount rules, approval thresholds, and playbooks, converting recurring exceptions into documented policy.

  • Drive deal health across the funnel: discount discipline, price realization, deal structure, and win rate by segment, diagnosing where deals leak value and fixing it.

  • Translate customer segmentation into differentiated pricing guidance and deal strategies, partnering with Sales to get it applied in real deals, and getting it into the ruleset so it's applied consistently.

  • Coach reps on pricing confidence and value-based selling

  • Partner with Customer Success to adapt the pricing and deal playbook for consistency after the sale.

About you

  • Proven experience in a deal desk, pricing, commercial, revenue operations, or sales-strategy role, ideally in B2B SaaS or fintech. Experience standing up or scaling a deal desk or pricing process from scratch is a plus.

  • Strong analytical toolkit, including SQL and/or advanced spreadsheet modeling.

  • The ability to leverage AI to build a scalable Pricing Deal Desk model, or the appetite to learn it. The direction is a low-touch desk: the agent executes the rules, its output gets better as you correct it, and each additional deal costs less human attention than the last

  • Fluent in English; German or Dutch is a plus.

In addition, here are the skills and attributes we are looking for:

  • Comfortable holding the line with Sales on discount governance while staying a genuine partner to the team.

  • A critical eye for AI output. The agent is sometimes confidently wrong, and catching that before a rep acts on it is part of the job.

  • Brings commercial judgment: understands how reps sell and how price sensitivity shifts across customer segments.

  • Structured and high-ownership, at ease in a fast, low-process, high-change environment.

  • Able to move fluidly between detailed data analysis and higher-level strategic thinking.

About Moss

Moss is the Finance AI platform for Europe's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work.

Founded in Berlin and used by more than 5,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, Gusto and Auto1, Moss has raised €200+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. Moss is backed by the most renowned tech investors including Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Global Founders Capital, Cherry Ventures, A-Star and Portage.

We have a team of 300+ people from 50+ nationalities in 5 offices across Europe. Be part of a culture that thrives on impact and speed, where you can take bold moves, learn fast and accomplish more. We’re a place where you can fast track your career - here's what else to expect:

  • Top-of-market compensation package, including equity. 

  • Our vibrant offices are at the heart of our culture, where in-person time fuels collaboration and connection over weekly breakfasts and Friday demos.

  • Additional benefits include: 20 days “work from abroad”, 600EUR/GBP Learning & Development Budget, and other local benefits.

Unless stated otherwise, benefits apply to full-time positions (interns and working students receive a tailored package).

By applying for the above position, you will confirm that you have reviewed and agreed to our Data Privacy Policy.

title: Werkstudent*in bei CORRECTIV.Exile
description:
Über die Stelle

Du möchtest dich für Pressefreiheit und eine aufgeklärte Gesellschaft einsetzen und bringst Interesse an internationaler und interkultureller journalistischer Zusammenarbeit mit? Dann setze deine redaktionellen Fähigkeiten für CORRECTIV.Exile ein.

CORRECTIV.Exile unterstützt Journalist*innen im Exil und schafft Plattformen für ihre Stimmen und ihre Arbeit. Ein zentraler Teil davon ist redaktionelle und mediale Zusammenarbeit: Wir begleiten exilierte Journalist*innen bei Recherchen, unterstützen sie beim Fact-Checking und bei der Aufbereitung ihrer Geschichten für ein deutschsprachiges Publikum.

Für diese besondere Arbeit suchen wir ab dem 01. Oktober 2026 eine*n Werkstudent*in zunächst befristet auf ein Jahr (mit Aussicht auf Verlängerung), die*der redaktionell und medial mit unserer Exile-Community zusammenarbeitet. Die wöchentliche Arbeitszeit beträgt 15 bis 20 Stunden in der Woche (max. 80 im Monat).


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du unterstützt exilierte Journalist*innen bei der redaktionellen Aufbereitung, Recherche und dem Fact-Checking ihrer Beiträge.
  • Du hilfst bei der Übersetzung sowie sprachlichen Bearbeitung von Texten aus dem Englischen ins Deutsche und stellst journalistische und stilistische Qualität sicher.
  • Du recherchierst eigenständig zu Themen rund um Pressefreiheit, Exiljournalismus und die Arbeit der Community.
  • Du unterstützt bei der Verifikation von Quellen, Daten und Fakten für Veröffentlichungen.
  • Du bringst dich in die Vor- und Nachbereitung von Talk-Formaten, Workshops sowie anderen Veranstaltungen ein und unterstützt vor Ort bei der Umsetzung (1-2 Abende pro Monat, in Berlin).
  • Du stehst im engen Austausch mit der Community der Exilmedien, um ihre journalistischen Anliegen und Bedürfnisse zu verstehen und redaktionell zu unterstützen.


Das bringst du mit

  • Du bist an einer Universität oder Fachhochschule eingeschrieben (gültige Immatrikulationsbescheinigung).
  • Du verfügst über verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie sehr gute Englischkenntnisse (mind. C1); weitere Fremdsprachen sind immer eine Bereicherung.
  • Du hast erste praktische Erfahrung im journalistischen oder redaktionellen Bereich – z. B. durch Volontariate, Praktika, freie Mitarbeit, Uni-Zeitung oder eigene Veröffentlichungen (bspw. Artikel, Recherchen, Reportagen o. Ä.).
  • Du hast erste Erfahrungen mit oder ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an Fact-Checking und journalistischer Verifikationsarbeit.
  • Du arbeitest sauber und präzise, mit einem guten Gespür für journalistische Sorgfalt und Quellenkritik.
  • Du bist interkulturell sensibel und interessiert an der Arbeit mit Exilmedien-Communities.
  • Du bist motiviert, die Ziele von CORRECTIV.Exile aktiv mitzugestalten und dich für Pressefreiheit einzusetzen.


Das bieten wir

  • Ein motiviertes, internationales Team mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen, das sich auf dich und deine Unterstützung freut.
  • Die Möglichkeit dich und deine Ideen proaktiv in einem gesellschaftlich relevanten Projekt einzubringen und aktiv an Pressefreiheit und Demokratie mitzuwirken.
  • Ein Gehalt zwischen 16 und 20 Euro/Stunde – abhängig von deiner Vorerfahrung.
  • Die Möglichkeit, deine Arbeitszeiten weitestgehend flexibel einzuteilen, passend zu deinem Studium und deinen Bedürfnissen - Homeoffice ist in Absprache teilweise möglich.
  • Regelmäßige Entwicklungsgespräche sowie die Möglichkeit, redaktionelle Verantwortlichkeiten zu erweitern.
  • Unmittelbare Einblicke in die Arbeit mit Journalist*innen im Exil und internationale Netzwerke.


So bewirbst du dich

Sende uns bitte bis zum 13. September 2026 deinen Lebenslauf (möglichst ohne Foto), Arbeitsproben (wenn vorhanden, z. B. veröffentlichte Artikel, Recherchen oder Textproben) und ein kurzes Motivationsschreiben, in dem du auf folgende Fragen eingehst:

  • Welche journalistische oder redaktionelle Erfahrung bringst du mit, etwa im Schreiben, im Recherchieren oder beim Fact-Checking?
  • Was macht für dich einen sorgfältig recherchierten und faktengeprüften Beitrag aus? Worauf legst du bei journalistischer Arbeit besonderen Wert?
  • Welche Veröffentlichung eines Exilmediums/Exiljournalisten hat dich zuletzt begeistert und warum?
​​​Wir behalten uns vor, bereits im Ausschreibungszeitraum erste Gespräche mit Bewerbenden zu führen.

Falls du noch Fragen zur Stelle hast, kontaktiere gerne Viera Zuborova.

title: Senior Business Intelligence Lead (all genders)
description:
Your Mission

EV charging is evolving from a niche technology into everyday infrastructure. As reev grows, teams increasingly need reliable, consistently defined metrics. Today, different dashboards, reporting dates, filters, and assumptions can produce different answers to the same business question. 
This role addresses the problem - not by building more dashboards, but by creating a shared and trustworthy data foundation. The goal is to establish clear definitions and consistent metrics so that teams and leadership can make informed decisions based on the same numbers. Someone who understands that unclear definitions, rather than a lack of data, are often the real problem can make a significant impact in this role. You own the certified layer, the single, agreed upon version of every core metric that reev runs on. You connect the definition, the data model, and the delivery. And when two numbers disagree, you are the person who says which one to trust. 

What you will do 

  • Define core metrics with Finance, Product, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Engineering, and Platform.
  • Agree on definitions, data contracts, and ownership forcore metrics with the teams that own them.
  • Maintain and verify the certified data layer, built in ETL tooland surfaced in Metabase, so teams can build their own dashboards on top of it.
  • Use SQL to validate data, investigate inconsistencies, and trace numbers back to their sources.
  • Work with Platform team to identify potential improvements in data flows, pipelines, and transformations, advise on next steps, and help prioritize next steps during planning.
  • Help stakeholders decide which number to trust when reports disagree.
  • Improve data literacy through practical guidance, workshops, and clear documentation.
  • Use AI-assisted tools for analysis, documentation, automation, and workflows. Check the results carefully.
 
What this role is not 
You will not be the central owner of every dashboard request. Teams remain responsible for their own dashboards, analyses, and data models built on their data contracts. This is also not a classic infrastructure or people-management role. 



What you bring along

Must-have 

  • Senior experience in BI, analytics, or data. Scale-up experience is helpful.
  • Strong SQL skills.You can read and write SQL,validate data, and trace where a number comes from.
  • Experience defining KPIs with Finance and other business owners.
  • Experience with data models, data quality, or data governance.
  • A good understanding of data flows, pipelines, and transformations.
  • Confidence working with senior stakeholders and challenging unclear or incorrect numbers.

You do not need every tool on the list. We care most about strong SQL, sound data thinking, and the ability to bring people to one shared definition.

Our Munich office at Stiglmaierplatz is an important place for collaboration. For this role, we expect at least three days on-site each week.

title: Senior Python Engineer, Platform Libraries (m/f/d)
description:
The role

We’re looking for a Senior Python Engineer, Platform Libraries (m/f/d) to join our team and play a key role in developing software that connects and translates lab equipment hardware interfaces, automates machines, and powers our next-generation automation platform. As a core team member, you will be working on cutting-edge technology, building software that bridges the gap between software and hardware, enabling seamless integration across various vendors.

Connectors are how we do it. Every instrument we bring online gets one, and every connector is built on our shared Python libraries: Bus, our Connector Development Kit, and the stack underneath them.

Our mission is to empower researchers and engineers by bridging the gap between lab equipment and cloud-based automation. Our customers are solving critical challenges like curing diseases, developing sustainable materials, and addressing global food security. We provide them with the tools to connect their devices, automate workflows, and unlock new possibilities in R&D.

Your mandate has two halves. Own the libraries as a product with real users, our own engineers today and external contributors later. And stay close enough to customer connector work that what you build is grounded in problems that actually exist.


Why you'll love this role

Your users are engineers. Your success lets other people ship connectors faster. That's a different craft from shipping features, and it's the one we're hiring for.

Real hardware, real failure modes. Instruments time out, return garbage, and arrive with documentation that's wrong. You'll debug against physical devices in our Munich workshop.


Open source on purpose. Our CDK and our standardization work (SiLA 2) are public. What you build gets used and criticized by people outside the company.


Senior scope, small team. You'll be the person who decides how connector engineering works here. No layer between you and that decision.


Your mission

1. The Builder: own the shared libraries

  • Own Bus, the CDK, and the core stack. Features, tests, CI, releases, and deprecations across the connectors already running in production.

  • Extract abstractions from real work. When the same pattern shows up in the third connector, it becomes a library feature. You're the one who notices, and the one who does it.

  • Make the docs good enough to remove yourself. An outside contributor should be able to build a connector on our libraries without a call.

  • Set the quality standard. You define what "tested" means before a connector reaches a customer, and you make it stick.

2. The Shipper: build connectors on real instruments

  • Ship production connectors end to end. Spec sheet, physical device, protocol, proof of connectivity, tested connector, live customer. Independently.

  • Reverse-engineer what isn't documented. Roughly half the instruments we touch have incomplete or wrong docs. Packet captures, trial and error, vendor calls.

  • Work with the workshop. Our Connector Factory team gets instruments development-ready. You take it from there.

  • Talk to the people who use it. Automation engineers and scientists at biotech and pharma customers. Their constraints shape what the libraries need next.


Your profile

  • Deep Python: 5+ years of writing production Python other people depend on. Async, typing, packaging, testing. You've designed APIs that other engineers built on, not just glue code.

  • You've debugged a real protocol against real hardware: gRPC, serial, TCP, OPC UA, CAN, USB. Which one matters less than having sat with a packet capture and a device that won't respond.

  • You ship without a spec: When the documentation is wrong, you reverse-engineer, instead of filing a vendor ticket and waiting. 

  • You build for other developers: An SDK, a library, an internal platform. Something where your job was making other engineers faster.

  • Located in Munich: The instruments are physically here at WERK1. 


Nice to have

  • SiLA 2, or another device abstraction and interoperability standard

  • Lab automation, scientific instruments, or a life science background

  • Open source maintainership with actual external contributors

  • C, C++, .NET, or Rust, for the vendor DLLs and drivers we end up wrapping

  • Docker, Kubernetes, edge deployment

  • German, for vendor conversations


Probably not a fit if

Better to say this now than in week 6.


  • Your Python is all APIs and databases and you've never debugged a physical device.

  • You'd want two quarters to redesign the library architecture before shipping a connector.

  • You like shipping integrations but have no appetite for going back afterwards to generalise, test, and document.

  • You want the library work without the customer deadlines. Both are in the job.


About UniteLabs

UniteLabs is on the mission to accelerate scientific progress by automating lab processes with scalable infrastructure.

We’re a startup based in Munich, Germany, pioneering an industry-first integration platform for lab automation, bridging hardware and software across vendor barriers to revolutionize life science R&D. By digitalizing life science R&D, we enable researchers in biotech, pharma, chemistry, and food industries to accelerate their work in groundbreaking fields such as disease treatment, sustainable materials, and food security.

Our platform empowers customers to analyze more data, run autonomous experiments, and leverage AI-driven solutions, driving innovation and efficiency. At UniteLabs, we are committed to providing the infrastructure that powers the future of scientific discovery.

As one of the first full-time hires, you'll thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and take on significant responsibilities from day one. We are a tech-driven company that takes pride in our solutions—and we’re looking for individuals who share that passion and want to grow with the company into leadership and expert roles.


Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Impactful Work: Work on meaningful products in an ambitious, supportive environment as part of a team revolutionizing connectivity in laboratory automation to enable breakthroughs in science and technology.

  • Work with the Best: Join a talented, ambitious team in a dynamic, transparent environment where your ideas help shape the company's future.

  • Collaborative Culture: Team-oriented environment focused on continuous knowledge-sharing and professional growth, with regular team-building activities including offsites and work-cations.

  • Flexible Environment: Backed by an employee-first culture that supports flexible remote work and PTO, with our main office in the vibrant WERK1 Munich hub. Hardware debugging happens there, so being regularly onsite is a must.

  • Attractive Compensation Package: Competitive compensation with growth potential in a VC-backed startup, along with a laptop of choice, annual productivity budget, and a growing list of benefits for sports, mobility, insurance, and more.


Tech stack

A non-exhaustive list of our main technologies and tools used for a given task:

  • Connectors: Python, SiLA 2, gRPC, zeroconf

  • Workflows: Python, Prefect

  • Services: TypeScript, NestJS, Prisma

  • Web: TypeScript, Vue 3, Nuxt 3, TailwindCSS

  • Cloud: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, AWS, Terraform

  • Databases: PostgreSQL


How to apply

If you’re passionate about automation, have a customer-focused mindset, and are ready to define the future of smart labs, we’d love to hear from you. Share your CV or LinkedIn profile, along with your responses to the three questions in the application form.

Let’s build the future of lab automation together. Apply today!

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
⭐️ Your Impact:

The European trades are one of the least digitised industries left. Software
penetration sits under 15%, against roughly 70% in the US. The labour
productivity gap runs about 30%. Millions of skilled people spend their evenings
on paperwork instead of the craft they trained for — in the industry that has to
deliver the energy transition.

There is almost no incumbent software to displace. That is unusual, and it won't
last.

smalt replaces the back office entirely rather than selling Meister another tool
to manage. In the last six months that went from a partner app and a dashboard
to around thirty AI agents in production - pricing real jobs, qualifying real
leads, running the operations of businesses whose payroll depends on it working.

These days building thirty agents is easy. Knowing which thirty is what's challenging.

That only comes from being in the Betrieb and talking to the Handwerker.

That's what this role is for.

What you'll do

You'll sit in Handwerksbetrieben - at the Meister's desk, in the van, on site, next to our team -
and watch how the work actually happens. Then you'll come back and build the
thing that fixes it, often multiple times on the same day.

- Spend real time with partners. Not a quarterly customer call. You'll know
  our Meister by name, understand their P&L, and notice the thing they've
  stopped complaining about because they assume it can't be fixed.
- Build across the stack. Python/FastAPI services, Vue interfaces, Flutter
  screens, agent loops, data pipelines - whatever the problem needs.
- Own agents in production. Not demos. Agents that price real jobs, answer
  real customers, and cost real money when they're wrong. Reliability,
  evaluation, structured output, graceful failure.
- Decide what to build. You'll write your own acceptance criteria. Nobody
  here will hand you a spec, and waiting for one is how to fail in this
  role.
- Measure whether it worked. Hours saved per partner, offers that go out
  untouched, leads answered before a competitor picks up. If the number didn't
  move, it didn't work.

What that looks like in practice

title: UVC Partners: Data & AI - Master Thesis / Internship (f/m/x)
description:
About us

UVC Partners is one of Europe’s leading early-stage venture capital firms. With our fourth fund generation of €250 million, we invest in disruptive B2B startups at the seed and Series A stage across Europe. Our focus areas include enterprise software, mobility, and industrial technologies.
Headquartered in Munich and closely integrated with UnternehmerTUM, Europe’s largest entrepreneurship center, we are proud partners to some of Europe’s most ambitious founders – including Flixbus, Isar Aerospace, finn.auto, Proxima Fusion, and Aleph Alpha.

At UVC Partners, we’re driven by a deep passion for entrepreneurship and its power to positively shape society. Environmental and social responsibility are core to our DNA. We hold ourselves to the highest standards in everything we do. As a firm, we continuously reinvent ourselves to stay ahead and best serve our portfolio and investors. We believe in ownership over hierarchy and foster a culture built on collaboration, curiosity, and personal engagement. And while we’re serious about our mission, we also genuinely enjoy working together and building lasting relationships along the way.


Your mission

You will join a specialized team working at the intersection of applied research and venture capital, side by side with investors, AI researchers, and engineers building the backbone of our investment intelligence. This is a hands-on role with real stakes. You will be treated as a full member of the team, expected to take a research question from literature to a working prototype and to present your results to the people who make the investment decisions.


Your profile

  • You are enrolled in a Master’s program in Computer Science, Data Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, or a similar program at a top university.
  • You bring depth, or the ambition to build it, in at least one relevant toolkit, whether that is graph ML and graph databases (e.g. PyTorch Geometric), LLM tooling, tool use and evaluation, or probabilistic modeling (e.g. PyMC, NumPyro).
  • You write clean, modular Python and have firm machine learning and statistics fundamentals.
  • You are fluent with AI-assisted coding tools and you have judgment about them. You know what they do well, where they quietly fail, and you review everything they produce. You do not ship AI slop.
  • You work independently. You have run a project where you set the direction yourself, and you can point to it.
  • You are fluent in English, including technical language. It is what you will work, write, and present in. German is helpful but not required.

How we work
We are an AI-powered development team. Everyone here codes with AI assistance, and we treat that as a craft. You need to know which parts of a problem to hand over, where these tools fail quietly, and how to review output you did not write.
Agency matters a lot in our team. You get mentorship, context, and access to everyone. You do not get someone assigning you tasks every morning. Take a rough problem statement, come back with an approach, show drafts while they can still change, and flag what is not working. What you bring should outweigh what it costs us to support you.

Potential Research Directions
These are directions we could explore, with scope defined together at the start based on your background and where the work leads.
1. With Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) we would work on a graph-structured database, where people and companies are nodes and the relationships between them are part of the data, and ask what that structure can tell us that a table cannot.
2. With Program-aided Language Models (PAL) we would have the model write a small program for every number it pulls from decks and financial statements, so figures are accurately computed, because that is what makes it safe to point a language model at financial data.
3. And with Bayesian Updating we would keep our recorded understanding of a company moving as new evidence arrives, since the investment process is iterative and a view written down two years ago should not still be the view today. Your thesis could focus on one of these, though as a full-time member of the team you will work across several.

Academic Supervision: The Lead of the Data & AI Team is a PhD candidate at TUM's School of Computation, Information and Technology (CIT) and can supervise CIT masters students directly, so there is no separate supervisor search. However, you are free to choose your own supervisor and candidates from other universities bring their own.


What we offer

  • Network: A desk at the Munich Urban Colab, our main office, with the option of a second one in Garching, plus access to the UnternehmerTUM ecosystem of startups, experts, and investors.
  • Team & Culture: Monthly team lunches, our regular Stammtisch, free sports classes, Makerspace access for your personal projects, and regular team events.
  • Compensation: An attractive salary for the full six months of your master thesis or internship.
  • Ownership: Research that is yours end to end and feeds real fund decisions.
  • Equipment: A MacBook or a Windows laptop, whichever you work best on.
  • AI Tooling: Full access to the AI development stack we use daily, and a team that will teach you to use it properly.
  • Real Data: Proprietary venture data that researchers rarely get access to, with the pipelines to use it productively.

Interested?
Please send a one-page CV, a current transcript, and a link to your GitHub or portfolio. Tell us which of these directions interests you most and why. We look forward to hearing from you!


Diversity is important to us

Diversity enriches our team. We explicitly encourage all qualified individuals to apply, regardless of gender, social and ethnic background, sexual orientation, religion, age, or disability.


Contact

Unternehmertum Venture Capital Partners GmbH , c/o Munich Urban Colab, Freddie- Mercury-Straße 5, 80797 Munich, Germany

www.uvcpartners.com

UVC Partners is an equal opportunity employer.

UVC Partners is an independent venture capital fund. For efficiency, we use certain shared services from UnternehmerTUM. This is why parts of the application process may appear UTUM-branded, and your application will be processed by UVC Partners and UnternehmerTUM.

title: Senior Lead, Government Innovation and Economic Growth
description:
The Role's Purpose

Plexal operates at the intersection of government, industry and emerging technology, helping organisations turn innovation ambition into practical capability, adoption and measurable impact.
 
The Senior Lead, Government Innovation & Economic Growth will play a critical role in shaping and delivering Plexal's growth across government. This is a nationally focused role responsible for identifying, shaping and securing high-value opportunities across central government, public sector organisations and strategic partners.
 
Based in the North West, the role will help position Plexal at the forefront of the UK's evolving government and innovation landscape. As government influence, investment and decision-making become increasingly distributed beyond Whitehall, the role will help Plexal identify and capitalise on emerging opportunities across government, economic growth, public sector reform, innovation adoption and place-based investment.
 
The successful candidate will combine strong commercial leadership with deep government insight, helping Plexal understand where policy, funding and customer priorities are moving and translating those trends into strategic opportunities, partnerships and sustainable revenue growth.
 
This is a hands-on commercial leadership role combining business development, strategic relationship management, proposition development and opportunity leadership, while also acting as a senior advisor to the wider GTM and leadership teams.


What You'll Do

  • Government Growth & Opportunity Leadership
    • Identify, prioritise and lead the pursuit of high-value opportunities across UK government. 
    • Build and maintain senior relationships across government departments, agencies, arm's-length bodies and wider public sector organisations. 
    • Shape early-stage opportunities by aligning customer priorities, policy developments and commercial propositions. 
    • Lead complex multi-stakeholder pursuits from early engagement through to contract award. 
    • Navigate government procurement and commercial environments, ensuring Plexal is well positioned to maximise success. 
    • Develop and maintain a strong understanding of government priorities, funding mechanisms and investment strategies to identify future opportunities ahead of formal procurement.
  • Market Intelligence & Strategic Positioning
    • Develop deep insight into emerging government priorities including economic growth, innovation adoption, AI, cyber resilience, public sector reform, science and technology, and place-based investment. 
    • Translate policy, market and customer insight into actionable growth opportunities for Plexal. 
    • Help shape Plexal's understanding of where government priorities, investment and demand are evolving. 
    • Identify emerging markets, funding streams and policy-driven opportunities that align with Plexal's strategic objectives. 
    • Position Plexal as a trusted partner capable of helping government translate ambition into adoption and measurable impact.
  • Cross-Government Go-To-Market Leadership
    • Shape and co-own Plexal's cross-government go-to-market strategy. 
    • Identify priority growth areas, departments and opportunity themes aligned to Plexal's strengths. 
    • Support the development and refinement of propositions that respond to changing government needs. 
    • Build repeatable approaches to opportunity identification, qualification and pursuit. 
    • Strengthen commercial discipline and opportunity management across the organisation. 
    • Support the creation of scalable propositions that can be applied across multiple government customers and sectors.
  • Strategic Relationship Management & Ecosystem Development
    • Act as a senior external representative for Plexal across government, industry and innovation ecosystem engagements. 
    • Build trusted relationships with senior government leaders, policy makers, commercial stakeholders and delivery partners. 
    • Establish Plexal as a credible voice within conversations around innovation, technology adoption, economic growth and government transformation. 
    • Build relationships across emerging government and innovation ecosystems outside London as government investment and decision-making continues to evolve. 
    • Represent Plexal at senior meetings, industry forums, conferences and government-facing events.
  • Partnerships & Growth Enablement
    • Develop strategic relationships with consultancies, technology providers, universities, ecosystem partners and delivery organisations. 
    • Build and shape consortium opportunities where partner-led approaches strengthen Plexal's position. 
    • Support priority bids, negotiations and commercial pursuits across the wider organisation. 
    • Share best practice across government sales, account development and opportunity shaping. 
    • Mentor and support colleagues across the commercial and delivery teams to strengthen capability and confidence.
  • KPIs and Commercial Outcomes
    • Significant £m pipeline generated and influenced across government markets. 
    • Material revenue secured through direct and partner-led opportunities. 
    • Number and quality of strategic opportunities shaped prior to procurement. 
    • Growth in multi-year and repeatable revenue opportunities. 
    • Conversion rate improvement across priority pursuits. 
    • Growth in partner-led opportunities and consortium wins. 
    • Strength and depth of senior relationships across government and strategic partners.
    • Contribution to Plexal's long-term positioning across government innovation, adoption and economic growth markets.


Your Skills

  • Commercially driven, outcome-focused and highly proactive. 
  • Naturally curious about government priorities, policy developments and market trends. 
  • Highly credible operating at senior levels across government and industry. 
  • Strong relationship builder with the ability to influence and align diverse stakeholder groups. 
  • Strategic thinker capable of translating insight into action. 
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and shaping undefined opportunities. 
  • Collaborative and committed to enabling the success of others. 
  • Resilient, adaptable and able to thrive in fast-moving environments.


Your Experience

Essential:

  • Proven track record of selling into UK government and winning complex public sector opportunities. 
  • Demonstrable success securing and growing contracts valued at £1m+ and/or multi-year engagements. 
  • Strong understanding of government procurement, commercial processes and public sector buying environments. 
  • Experience building relationships with senior government stakeholders. 
  • Strong commercial acumen including opportunity shaping, negotiation and deal strategy. 
  • Experience developing and executing go-to-market strategies in complex environments. 
  • Experience working with partners to shape and deliver consortium bids and strategic opportunities. 
  • Ability to operate effectively across strategy, relationship management and hands-on opportunity delivery. 
  • Strong understanding of the relationship between government policy, funding, investment priorities and commercial opportunity.
 
Highly desirable:
  • Experience working across multiple government departments or policy domains. 
  • Understanding of economic growth, devolution, place-based investment and public sector reform. 
  • Experience within innovation, technology, consulting, digital transformation, cyber or AI-related environments. 
  • Experience identifying and developing opportunities arising from policy change, government reform and market shifts. 
  • Existing network across UK government, strategic partners and innovation ecosystems. 
  • Experience operating within high-growth, entrepreneurial or scaling organisations. 
  • Familiarity with government priorities relating to AI adoption, cyber resilience, science and technology, productivity and economic growth.


Who You Are

  • Open to UK Nationals who hold or are eligible for Security Check (SC) clearance. (See more on clearance eligibility.)
  • Degree-level education or equivalent professional experience
  • Relevant commercial, consulting or public sector credentials are advantageous
  • Commitment to Plexal’s values of diversity, equity, and inclusion


Why us?

As a start-up, we thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced work environment dedicated to empowering innovators. We embrace individuals who leverage technology and creativity to tackle our greatest challenges head-on. We strongly advocate for maintaining a harmonious work-life balance, our goal is to ensure every member of our team can authentically be themselves and live their best lives. title: Sales Account Executive - Enterprise, UKI (m/f/d)
description:
What is Jedox?

Jedox is a global leader in Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) and a recognized Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader, helping organizations transform fragmented planning into connected, data-driven decision-making.

Trusted by more than 2,500 customers worldwide, Jedox enables business planning, budgeting and forecasting for finance, sales, and broader enterprise departments with leading-edge technology to outperform digital transformation and provide tangible customer value. At the heart of the platform is JedoxAI - a multi-agent intelligence engine delivering explainable, AI-powered forecasting, natural-language insights and AIssisted™ planning - putting Jedox at the forefront of the shift to AI-driven performance management.


Your Responsibilities

As a Sales Account Executive (m/f/d) within the Jedox team, you will play a key part in helping enterprise customers to transform their planning, forecasting and performance management processes. Acting as a trusted advisor, you will use a value-based sales approach to show how Jedox provides modern, digital and integrated enterprise performance and analysis (xP&A) solutions.

In this role, you will own the entire sales process for enterprise customers, from identifying potential clients to closing deals. You will promote Jedox as the ideal solution for xP&A initiatives, work closely with internal teams and develop long-term relationships with customers and partners, while maintaining a strong focus on value, trust and sustainable success.

We are building a high-performing team defined by ownership, accountability and energy. This is a genuinely exciting time to join: AI is reshaping how every finance team plans and forecasts, and Jedox is right at the centre of that conversation - giving you a fresh, differentiated story to take to market. If you're a motivated seller who enjoys being out in front of customers and partners, and want to make your mark in an exciting company, you'll find real support, momentum and opportunity here. You will own your number, your territory and your pipeline - creating opportunity rather than waiting for it, with a team around you that celebrates the wins together.

  • Own the end-to-end sales cycle: Generate revenue by adopting a value-selling approach throughout the process, from initial engagement to closing enterprise-level deals - with full personal accountability for every outcome in your territory.
  • Create and own high-quality pipeline: Build and maintain healthy pipeline coverage against your quota through proactive, self-generated prospecting - not just inbound - with disciplined weekly pipeline management in our CRM as the single source of truth.
  • Communicate the value of Jedox: Demonstrate how Jedox and JedoxAI empower xP&A projects and elevate planning, forecasting and business decisions - bringing AI-driven, explainable forecasting into the conversation and anchoring every discussion on business outcomes, not features.
  • Inspire digital transformation: Engage prospects by presenting a clear and compelling vision of digitisation and integrated business planning.
  • Develop strategic sales plans: Identify, prospect and execute targeted sales plays and activities to win enterprise customers, including structured account planning, rigorous qualification (e.g. MEDDPICC) and multi-threading across finance, IT and operations stakeholders.
  • Cross-functional collaboration: Acquire new customers by working closely with the pre-sales, channel management, marketing and business development teams - bringing colleagues and partners in early, and lifting each other up as one team with one number.
  • Drive market-facing activity: Contribute to workshops, webinars and events alongside marketing and partners to create demand and build visible expertise in your market.
  • Work smarter with AI: Actively use modern AI tools in your daily workflow - from account research and prospecting to preparing presentations, proposals and follow-ups - so more of your time goes where it counts: in front of customers and partners.
  • Own forecasting and pipeline management: Maintain accurate monthly and quarterly forecasts as well as pipeline reports, with strong CRM hygiene, and play an active role in prospecting activities.
  • Build lasting relationships: Build trusted partnerships with customers, partners and internal stakeholders to ensure long-term success.


Your Profile

  • Over three years' experience in professional sales, ideally within the FP&A function.
  • Experience in Enterprise Performance Management or in selling analytics, AI, data, or ERP solutions.
  • Strong record of success in achieving and exceeding sales goals.
  • Proven ability to build, manage and self-generate a healthy sales pipeline and expand existing accounts.
  • A high-ownership mindset: you act with urgency, take responsibility for your results, and when challenges arise you come with ideas on how to tackle them together.
  • Resilience and positivity: you're the kind of person who stays positive, keeps going and enjoys the journey as much as the win.
  • A love of being active in the market: you genuinely enjoy talking to customers and partners - on calls, in meetings and at events - and you know that's where great pipeline comes from.
  • Strong collaboration skills with a clear focus on customer success and innovation.
  • Confident, hands-on use of AI tools (such as Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or similar) in your day-to-day selling - for example researching accounts, building presentations and business cases, sharpening messaging and working smarter across the sales cycle.
  • Native or fluent English skills; an established network and knowledge of the UK & Ireland enterprise market are a real advantage.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Bookkeeper — Lab54

Location: London. All 3 days in office for the first three months. From month 4, 1 day per week remote once the agreed targets are being met.

Shape: Part-time, 3 days per week. Permanent or contract — both considered.

Salary: £30–34k FTE equivalent, pro-rata (£18–20.5k at 3 days). Contract equivalent £150–200 per day.

Reports to: Financial Controller (interim: Managing Director)

Start: As soon as available

About Lab54

Lab54 is a content-led events and production company: [Anywhere But A Club.]

We create high-impact experiences in unexpected locations, capture them, and turn them into content. Combined global audience of 425,000+. We work with brands, record labels and artists — around 100 events a year across brand activations, artist pop-ups, hard-ticket shows, house parties and festival takeovers.

The role

The Bookkeeper is Lab54's day-to-day finance function: reconciliation, purchase-order matching, receipt capture, invoicing, debtor chasing and payroll preparation.

The defining feature of the job is that every pound has to land against an event. Lab54's core financial object isn't the month — it's the project. Each event carries a code (YYMM-Owner-Event-City) that runs from HubSpot through Xero, Teamwork and the purchase-order flow. Coding transactions to that project is not admin; it's the thing that makes per-event profitability computable. It is the single most important part of this role.

This role prepares, never approves. All payment runs are approved by the Managing Director, with the CEO approving above an agreed threshold.

Responsibilities

Purchase orders and supplier ledger

  • Match supplier invoices to their purchase order in Xero. This is a manual link, and it is the control that stops us paying more than we agreed.
  • Enforce the PO rule at the front door: any commitment of £500 or more needs a PO, and an invoice arriving without a PO number goes back to the supplier rather than into the ledger.
  • Prepare payment runs for approval. Nothing leaves the business without a bill, a PO and a sign-off.
  • Reconcile supplier statements monthly against our purchase ledger — the check that catches duplicate invoices and payments before they're made.
  • Maintain the purchase ledger and keep the aged creditor position accurate.

Reconciliation and coding

  • Bank and card reconciliations kept current within 48 hours, including Revolut Business card spend against Xero tracking categories.
  • Every reconciled line matched to a real source document. A line that reconciles without a bill behind it is an exception to raise, not a box to tick.
  • Code every transaction to the correct project code and tracking category. Chase the team when a code is missing rather than guessing one.
  • Keep the suspense and uncoded accounts at nil by month-end.
  • Produce a weekly untagged-spend report, by spender, and drive it to zero.

Receipts and VAT recovery

  • Chase and capture missing receipts to a 98% target. This is a cash exercise, not a filing one — every missing VAT invoice is input VAT we can't reclaim.
  • Flag transactions carrying no VAT treatment where the supplier is UK VAT-registered.
  • Prepare the VAT return workings for the external accountancy firm, who own submission.

Sales invoicing and debtors

  • Raise client invoices within 48 hours of the billing trigger, coded to the project.
  • Own debtor chasing end to end — a consistent cycle, escalated when it stalls, so nobody else in the business is carrying it.
  • Match incoming receipts to the right invoice and contact. Money that arrives against the wrong customer looks identical to money that never arrived.
  • Keep sales invoice sequencing clean — anything voided or reissued carries a recorded reason.

Project close

  • When a project closes, produce its final position: budgeted cost against actual cost, budgeted revenue against invoiced revenue, and the resulting margin.
  • Issue that to the CEO and Operations Director as a matter of routine. It is not a report anyone should have to request.
  • Late costs land after an event has finished — that's the nature of the business. The job is to make sure they land against the right project and that the closing number reflects them.

Cash and reporting

  • Produce a weekly cash one-pager: bank position, overdue debtors with days outstanding, payment runs due, projected balance.
  • Keep the company's master P&L model current — updating actuals and committed costs as they change, so the forecast reflects where the business genuinely is.
  • The model is ours; you update the numbers within it. Structural or formula changes come to the CEO first.

Payroll preparation

  • Prepare payroll data and submit it to the external payroll provider ahead of deadline.
  • Post the payroll journal to Xero each month. Wages must not sit in a control account.
  • Confirm the payroll account is funded before each run. This role does not execute payroll.

Close, deadlines and records

  • Run the monthly close to a published working-day deadline: accruals prepared with supporting detail, journals posted, period locked.
  • Every accrual carries a schedule — supplier, event, date of work. No balance we can't explain.
  • Maintain the statutory deadline register (VAT, PAYE, corporation tax, Companies House) and flag each one in advance. No filing sits invisibly in someone else's workflow.
  • Keep records orderly and audit-ready for the external accountancy firm.

What the first 90 days actually look like

We are being straight about this because we want someone who finds it interesting rather than alarming.

Lab54 has grown faster than its finance function, and we've recently changed accountants. The ledger carries a real backlog: untagged transactions across two financial years, unposted payroll journals, a month-end close that has not been run to a cadence, and a purchase-order process that has only just gone live. There is a documented correction schedule and an external FD working through it.

The first 90 days is a clean-up, not a steady state.

Days 1–30. Learn the ledger and the project-code structure. Take over reconciliation, receipt capture and PO matching. Get the weekly untagged report running.

Days 31–60. Clear the untagged backlog. Take over sales invoicing, debtor chasing and received-payment matching. Payroll preparation and the monthly payroll journal move across.

Days 61–90. Run a full month close to deadline: suspense at nil, every accrual scheduled, supplier statements reconciled. Per-project cost data becomes reportable for the first time.

After that it becomes a genuinely well-defined job inside a documented control structure — and you'll have built it.

On being in the office. The first three months are fully office-based, and that's deliberate rather than a policy position. Clearing a backlog this size means asking people questions in real time — whose card that was, what the missing PO covers, which event a supplier belongs to. That's an hour of work in a room and a week of work over email. From month 4, one of the three days moves to remote, provided the measures below are being met.

What we're looking for

Essential

  • Proven bookkeeping experience. Xero to a high standard is non-negotiable — tracking categories, purchase orders, bank rules, manual journals.
  • Purchase-order matching and supplier statement reconciliation as routine practice.
  • A project- or job-costing background — agency, events, production, construction, consultancy, anywhere the job rather than the month is the unit of profit. This is the part of the role we can't train quickly.
  • Strong reconciliation, coding and purchase-ledger discipline.
  • Experience preparing payroll data for an external provider and posting the payroll journal.
  • Comfortable working inside a defined control structure where you prepare and someone else approves.
  • Reliability over ambition. The value of this role is that nothing is ever late or missing.

Nice to have

  • Multi-currency invoicing and foreign supplier payments. We run events across Europe.
  • Dext, Revolut Business, or similar capture and expense tooling.
  • Experience cleaning up a ledger rather than only maintaining a tidy one.

How you'll work

  • Meticulous. Proactive on receipts, POs and debtors — chasing people is part of the job, not an escalation.
  • Willing to say when something doesn't look right. A number you can't explain is a question, not a rounding difference.
  • Discreet and trustworthy with company finances.

description:
We're Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world's healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

The role

Heidi's UK and Europe business is growing faster than the finance scaffolding underneath it. Central finance across Sydney, Melbourne and Manila runs month-end close, core accounting and day-to-day operations, but the region needs someone on the ground who owns the accuracy of its numbers and sits close enough to the commercial team to shape decisions before they get made. Today, regional leaders wait on Australian hours for answers about their own P&L. You'll end that.

The role has two halves and both carry equal weight. You'll own regional financial control and compliance: the integrity of the balance sheet, the accuracy of management reporting and forecasts, cash, strong local controls, and statutory obligations across Companies House, HMRC and VAT, directed through external advisers. You'll also be a hands-on business partner to UK and Europe leadership, Sales and Customer Success, owning the P&L narrative, bringing a commercial view to pricing, deal terms and customer economics, and making sure teams see the financial consequence of the choices they make. What you'll do

Financial reporting and month-end close

  • Own the integrity of the UK&Europe balance sheet, with reconciliations that stay current, reviewed and explainable

  • Be the single point of contact for group finance on anything UK&Europe: queries, adjustments, restatements, consolidation-level questions

Compliance and risk oversight

  • Own the UK&Europe compliance calendar (Companies House, HMRC, VAT) by directing external accountants and advisers

  • Own the adviser relationships (accounting, tax, audit), keeping work well scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi's internal finance standards

  • Build an early-warning process so compliance risk is caught and escalated well before it threatens trading status

  • Be the accountable owner if something in the compliance chain breaks down

Commercial business partnering

  • Be the day-to-day finance partner to UK&Europe leadership, owning the regional P&L narrative, budget vs actual and the "why" behind the numbers

  • Bring a commercial lens to pricing, deal terms and customer economics, flagging risk and opportunity early

  • Translate regional performance into clear, decision-ready input for FP&A and company leadership

  • Give UK&Europe business leaders a reliable, self-serve view of their numbers, so decisions stop waiting on Australian hours

  • Feed central finance the regional inputs it needs at close: accrual estimates, revenue and spend context, then review and sign off on the UK&Europe result

Revenue risk and collections

  • Partner with Sales and Customer Success to resolve aged and disputed balances and unblock stuck revenue

  • Own the commercial view of collection risk: which accounts, why, and what it means for cash, and feed it into forecasting

  • Drive down UK&Europe DSO by fixing the upstream causes (contracting, disputes, process), not by chasing invoices

FinOps, controls and performance frameworks

  • Build the operating rhythm that turns UK&Europe finance from reactive support into a reliable performance framework: clear KPIs, owners, review cadences and escalation paths

  • Partner with budget owners on spend decisions before they are made, rather than policing them after the fact

  • Strengthen financial controls across spend, approvals, vendor onboarding, card usage, subscriptions and commercial commitments, while keeping the process pragmatic for a fast-moving region

  • Review regional AP and card activity, including prompt removal of leaver access and cards, and escalate anomalies to central finance operations

  • Partner with external accountants, tax advisers, compliance providers and other vendors, making sure work is well-scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi’s internal finance standards

  • Use FinOps-style discipline to connect spend, usage and outcomes, especially across tooling, GTM systems, implementation costs and region-specific operating expenses

  • Create simple documentation and control checks so the region can scale without relying on informal knowledge or one-off fixes

What you'll need

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen — comfortable moving between P&L narrative, deal economics and cash impact

  • Experience business partnering with Sales, Customer Success or regional leadership in a growth business

  • Track record improving collections or DSO by fixing root causes, not just process

  • Experience owning spend or expense controls in a way that supports the business rather than only governing it

  • Comfortable directing (not necessarily performing) statutory compliance and VAT work through external advisers

  • High degree of autonomy and ownership in a small, remote-first global finance team

  • Clear, confident communicator — able to hold your own with commercial leaders and external advisers alike

  • Experience in a multi-entity or multi-currency business

Nice to have

  • Experience in a high-growth SaaS or technology company

  • Qualified accountant (ACA / ACCA / CIMA or equivalent)

  • Exposure to Companies House, HMRC and Irish Revenue processes

  • Experience with Campfire, Airwallex or similar modern finance tooling

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You'll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we'd like to see. We're medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who've felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Building what we're building isn't always easy. But we didn't choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn't whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you're doing the defining work of your career.

We take care of you.

We offer comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a £100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a £500 home office budget, a £700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

Perk's revenue organisation is 800 people selling to more than 10,000 companies. Behind them sits a CRM, an enrichment and signal stack, a growing set of AI agents - and a lot of manual work that no longer needs to exist. Your job is to remove it and to build the automated systems that replace it.

You will own GTM Engineering end-to-end: which tools we use, how the architecture fits together, what gets built, and what it does for revenue. You report to the VP of Revenue Operations, lead a small senior team across Europe and North America, and work across SDR, Account Executive, and Account Management - a few high-impact projects each quarter.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it. You will be in Clay, in the orchestration logic, in the agent workflows, building alongside a team doing the same. You're using your experience to guide and coach them to accelerate the pace.

The other half of the job is commercial. The best GTM engineers we have met can sit with a regional Sales VP, work out why their pipeline isn't converting, and leave with the right thing to build. That instinct matters more to us than any single tool on a CV.

What You'll Do

Own the strategy and the stack

  • Define Perk's GTM engineering architecture - how CRM, enrichment, signal, sequencing, orchestration and data layers fit together.

  • Make the tooling calls: what we adopt, what we consolidate, what we retire, and why it pays for itself.

  • Set the roadmap with the VP of Revenue Operations, Sales leadership, and the Revenue Systems and Data teams.

  • Establish the standards the team builds to - version control, documentation, testing, and rollback.

Build, hands-on

  • Design and build in Clay: tables, waterfall enrichment, AI columns, webhooks and API integrations in production.

  • Own the orchestration layer - the logic deciding which records enter a workflow, when, and on what criteria. This is where GTM automation succeeds or fails.

  • Build agentic workflows on modern LLM and agent tooling to take research, qualification, summarisation and data entry off people entirely.

  • Write the code the job needs - Python, SQL, SOQL or TypeScript.

Automate across SDR, AE, and AM

  • Own account prospecting automation globally: TAM sourcing, enrichment, ICP and intent scoring, prioritisation and distribution.

  • Give AEs their selling time back - CRM autofill, quoting, meeting prep, opportunity hygiene, first outbounds.

  • Build account intelligence for Account Management: risk signals, whitespace, account planning.

  • Take each project from prototype to production properly - instrumented and validated before it scales.

Bridge commercial and technical

  • Turn commercial problems into technical architecture, and technical output into impact a revenue VPs recognises.

  • Understand Perk's revenue goals and how to leverage AI capabilities for us to achieve them quicker and more efficiently.

  • Understand and drive clear and tangible commercial outcomes. For example, how to reduce the time that quota-carrying roles spend on non-core activities such as account research, be able to quantify the impact, and clearly communicate the outcomes to leadership.

Build the team

  • Lead and grow a small, senior team across Europe and North America.

  • Set clear ownership, and the review discipline that makes shipping fast also means shipping safely.

  • Grow the team's technical depth and commercial judgement in equal measure.

What Will Make You Successful

Experience

  • Deep background across Revenue Operations, GTM Engineering, Sales Systems, Growth Engineering, or an adjacent technical commercial function in B2B SaaS

  • Proven track record in GTM Engineering specifically, with delivery at real scale — systems hundreds of sellers relied on, not a pilot for one team

  • Time as both a builder and a leader. This role needs both.

Technical craft

  • Clay expertise in production - complex tables, waterfall enrichment, webhook integrations and AI column logic that revenue teams actually depended on.

  • Deep Salesforce fluency: the data model, integration patterns, and where the constraints really are.

  • Working proficiency in code — Python, SQL, SOQL, TypeScript or equivalent. You pull your own data. Not all coding languages are necessary, but proficiency in one or some is required.

  • Architecture instincts: you build for scale, monitoring and recovery, not just for the first successful run.

  • Depth across several layers of the modern GTM stack - enrichment and data (Apollo, Clearbit, ZoomInfo, Cognism, PredictLeads), signal and intent (6sense, Bombora, UserGems), sequencing (Outreach, Salesloft), orchestration (n8n, Make, Workato), data infrastructure (Snowflake, dbt, BigQuery) and LLM and agent tooling. Nobody has all of it. We care that you have real depth somewhere and can learn the rest quickly.

Commercial instinct

  • You judge your work by whether it moved a commercial metric, not by whether it shipped.

  • You have the credibility with Sales leaders to scope the right build - and to say when automation is the wrong answer.

  • You understand the funnel end to end: TAM, ICP, pipeline generation, conversion, expansion, and the economics underneath.

Nice to have

  • Having stood up a GTM engineering function at a high-growth SaaS business, ideally above $100M ARR.

  • Experience taking an automation programme from pilot to global production, including what you learned when it got bumpy.

  • Multi-region GTM experience across EMEA and North America.

Why This Role

GTM Engineering is a discipline being written right now, and most companies are still treating it as a tooling function. This is the chance to own it properly, the stack, the architecture, the build, and the commercial outcome across a $300M+ revenue business with 800 people in the field, a genuine appetite for automation, and the budget and executive backing to move fast.

You would be the first person in this seat, with real systems and real data to work with rather than a blank page, and the freedom to decide what Perk's automation layer should look like. There is a lot to go after, the problems are interesting, and the impact is immediate and visible.

If you want to build the automation layer of a commercial engine at this scale and you want to still have your hands on it come and build it here.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.
